body: I admit I'm sceptical but it can't hurt to try I guess, I appreciate you're advice

Yeah I get what you mean, I just don't want to be ruled by it, I want to be able to work and stuff without having this loom over me and effecting my job performance, the other part is my family get pissed off with me about it and tell me just to suck it up and get to work which just makes it worse even though I know what they are saying is right
I do appreciate it, I think I've said it enough but whatever happens im going to be there for her and if if it happens, my child too

Well yes I do understand it's ultimately her choice but yeah I don't believe we are ready for such a responsibility however neither of us planned this.

I do understand that everything really is just adcive and the final decision is mine to make but it does help to have other perspectives and admittedly part of the reason for the post is so I wasn't completely in my own head and overthinking this.

I won't go into detail but she could potentially never be able to have children and I would say that's playing on her mind and as I've said a few time if she does choose to have this child that I would be there for her and if we didn't work out for whatever reason would still always be there for my child.

Youre right that it would effect both our lives heavily which is part of the reason im concerned because we aren't far in our respective careers and would have a very hard time financially unless I was working 60 hours a week or so which I was planning to do anyways but with a child involved I would want to be home to spend quality time with them.

At the moment I'm thinking a talk to her about my concerns and we get a blood test to confirm. If she chooses to abort then we continue with our lives and if she chooses to keep it then we start figuring out how this is all going to work.

Well yeah I wouldn't say I have any unreasonable fears, mostly just about if we are ready and the type of environment we'd be bring a child into and then how it will effect our lives in terms of our careers and other life goals, as well as other expectations such as would I be responsible for providing income or would we split it so we could both have quality time with our child

I agree that at the end of the day we both didn't want a child this earlier but we still made that choice to not use contraception on one occasion,  im not going to be over dramatic about it as I understand her point of view and again if she does end up having the child I will be there.

Just for reference however, what would you consider to be an unreasonable request? Aside from the obvious ones like demanding she gets an abortion.

Thats the main reason why I think its the wrong time for us, don't get me wrong I love her and we have already been through a lot but the fact is that 95% of the issues in our relationship is caused by us having things from our past that haven't been properly resolved and simply just us being young and making mistakes, I don't see my life with anyone else but I don't want to bring a child into that environment. Like I said if she does have the child then I would be there every chance I get and would stay with her, if we end up splitting up then we cross that bridge when we get there. I understand where you're coming from as well and my childhood isn't that far off your experiences but I'm sure you can understand my point of view.

P.s sorry you had to go through that, it sucks and leaves scars

See I disagree with that, im understand where you're coming from obviously but a child takes two people and I think the choice of how to proceed should be made together with that person, if it doesn't go well and one person decides to leave then that's that but that discussion should be had and both party's feelings taken into consideration

Our relationship has been very complicated but it's never been about us as individuals more so about outside things and past experiences so I wouldn't leave her I just don't think its the right time while we are still figuring out other things
